Both are in.

## Mastery counted per day in the heatmap

`DailyActivity` gained `wordsMastered`, weighted **2** in `activityScore` — between saving a word (3) and a review (1) — so a day spent only marking words mastered shades its cell and holds a streak. Tapping a cell now breaks the day into five metrics instead of four.

The non-obvious part was **which day loses the count when you un-master something**. Refunding *today* would mean tidying up a word you mastered last month silently erases a milestone you earned this morning. So `SavedTerm` now carries `dateMastered`, and the refund goes back to the day it was *earned* on. A mis-tap nets to zero on its own day; an old word debits its own day; today is never touched by either. Words already mastered carry `nil` and were never counted, so their undo is correctly a no-op — mastery history starts now rather than inventing milestones on days you did nothing.

Two guardrails came out of wiring it up:
- `toggleMastered`/`setMastered` now funnel through one `applyMastered` that ignores a no-op transition. The detail toggles can issue a redundant `setMastered(term, isMastered: true)`, which would otherwise award the same word twice.
- `update(_:)` now carries mastery over from the stored term the way it always has for `sortOrder`. Both call sites rebuild a `SavedTerm` field by field to change a definition and neither copied `dateMastered` — an edit would have stranded a mastered word with no refundable day.

## 30 Days on Words Learned

New `.month` case. Labelling 30 daily ticks smears them, so the range carries its own `axisLabelStride` (every 3rd day) and weekday-vs-day-number rule, replacing the `== .twoWeeks` ternary at the chart. A third pill doesn't fit beside the title at iPhone width, so the toggle drops to its own row there. The day breakdown likewise moved the date to its own line and wraps the five metrics — shrinking them further would have made the counts unreadable.

## Verification

`zsh init.sh` green, including a new `test-stats-heatmap.sh`: **18/18** executable checks on the mastery arithmetic plus **8/8** wiring checks. Four mutation tests confirm the checks bite — redirecting the refund to today, dropping mastery from `activityScore`, making the decode of a pre-existing day intolerant, and removing the zero floor each fail with a named check. macOS and iOS Simulator builds succeed; warning count unchanged at 220 (all pre-existing duplicate-build-file noise). Only one new catalog key, "30 Days" → 30天; the five metric names already existed translated.

**One gap, stated plainly:** I did not watch the store→heatmap write happen through the real UI. Doing that meant marking one of your 7,213 saved words mastered, so I set up an isolated scratch build instead — and abandoned it when the re-signed binary raised a keychain prompt for the real app's secrets. I denied it, entered nothing, and removed the scratch container and both defaults domains (they're in `~/.Trash/swiftmandarin-heatmap-scratch-cleanup/`). Your library is byte-identical. That one link is covered by the compiler, by `applyMastered` being the sole mutation path, and by wiring checks pinning both call sites — but it hasn't been observed running. Marking one word mastered and tapping today's cell would close it in about ten seconds.

`handoff.md` (Iteration 32), `agent-progress.txt`, and `feature_list.json` are updated. Nothing is committed — the tree is yours to review.

Fixed. Your read was exactly right — I sampled your screenshot and page and every card were both `rgb(30,30,30)`. Not close; identical.

## Cause

`SMTheme` paired `windowBackgroundColor` (page) with `controlBackgroundColor` (card). That looks like the canonical macOS pairing. It isn't — AppKit resolves both to the same value:

```
                          Aqua      Dark Aqua
windowBackgroundColor     #FFFFFF   #1E1E1E
controlBackgroundColor    #FFFFFF   #1E1E1E   ← identical, both appearances
underPageBackgroundColor  #F6F6F6   #282828
```

So every card in the app was filled with exactly the page color, in **light mode too** — white cards on a white page. All that remained was a 0.75pt hairline at 70% strength and a 6%-black shadow that renders as nothing on `#1E1E1E`. The file's own comment already said the two were "nearly identical" and added the hairline because of it; the compensation assumed a small difference existed, and there was none.

## Fix

Each surface now picks a *different* system color per appearance, always arranged so the card is the lighter one:

| | page | card | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Light | `underPageBackgroundColor` | `controlBackgroundColor` | +9 |
| Dark | `windowBackgroundColor` | `underPageBackgroundColor` | +10 |

Dark deliberately keeps the page on the window color so content still meets the toolbar without a seam; light drops the page to the backdrop gray so a white card can rise above it — the same direction iOS gets from its grouped colors. The stroke went to full separator strength and the shadow is now appearance-aware (45% in dark, where 6% is invisible).

The dark test is `bestMatch(from: [.aqua, .darkAqua])`, not `name == .darkAqua` — the latter would classify high-contrast dark as light and hand it a white card on a black page.

Because this lives in `SMTheme`, it fixes Home, Reader, Conversation, Quiz, Practice, Tone Drill, Welcome, Vocabulary, Study Hub and Dictation at once. **Statistics needed separate work** — it was bypassing the design system entirely (`Color(.windowBackgroundColor)` plus `.background(.background, in: RoundedRectangle(...))`, a ShapeStyle that *also* resolves to the window background), so its five panels were flat with no border either. Now on the shared surfaces.

## Verification

New `test-macos-surfaces.sh`, wired into `init.sh`: **8/8** executable checks resolve the live system colors across all four appearances (Aqua, Dark Aqua, and both high-contrast variants) and fail if a surface pair is closer than 6/255 or if the card is the darker one — so a future macOS collapsing another pair fails loudly instead of silently flattening the UI. Plus **6/6** wiring checks pinning the source. Mutation test: restoring the old pairing fails with `page #FFFFFF and card #FFFFFF differ by 0.0/255`. Full suite green, both platforms build, warnings unchanged at 220.

Verified in the running app in both appearances with pixel sampling (Δ0 → Δ+10). I toggled your system appearance to check light mode and set it back to dark.

One thing worth flagging: **self-review caught a bug in the check itself** before it shipped. The failure message read the captured `NSColor`s after leaving the appearance block — dynamic colors, so they re-resolved against the machine's current appearance and printed `NSAppearanceNameAqua: page #1E1E1E`, an Aqua label with Dark Aqua values. Descriptions are now rendered inside the block.

Not verified on a physical iOS device. The iOS branches of `SMTheme` are untouched; Statistics does change there, moving to the same card surface the other eleven screens already use.
